promptInstructions: Draft a complaint under Section 31 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, before the State RERA Authority.

NOTE TO INDIAN-COURTS-JSON: State RERA authorities must be mapped in indian-courts.json with their addresses (Bihar RERA - Patna, Jharkhand RERA - Ranchi, UP RERA - Lucknow + Gautam Buddh Nagar bench, Delhi RERA - Delhi, Maharashtra MahaRERA - Mumbai, Karnataka K-RERA - Bengaluru, etc.). Filing must be at the RERA where the project is located.

Form: Per State RERA Rules — typically Form 'M' (complaint by allottee) / Form 'N' (complaint by promoter) / Form 'O' (by real estate agent). Forms vary across states; default to Form M for individual allottee complaint.
Limitation: Act does not prescribe specific limitation for complaints, but cause of action must be live — generally treated under the Limitation Act 1963 by analogy.
Para 1: Parties — Complainant (allottee/association); Promoter (R-1) — definition under S.2(zk).
Para 2: Jurisdiction — S.20 + S.31 — State RERA where project is located. Filing fee per state Rules (e.g., Bihar RERA ₹1,000; UP RERA ₹1,000; MahaRERA ₹5,000 per unit).
Para 3: Project details — name, RERA registration number (S.3 mandatory registration), location, sanctioned plan, promised completion date.
Para 4: Allotment details — unit, agreement for sale (S.13 mandatory — agreement before accepting more than 10% of consideration), consideration, payments made.
Para 5: Promised vs actual possession — quantify delay in months. Cite Aftab Singh v. Emaar MGF (2019) NCDRC reaffirming RERA + Consumer concurrent jurisdiction.
Para 6-8: Factual narrative — chronology.
Para 9: Specific violations:
- S.11: Promoter functions (project disclosures + maintenance till conveyance);
- S.12: Liability for false / incorrect statements in advertisement / prospectus — allottee may claim refund + interest if induced;
- S.13: Mandatory agreement for sale (no more than 10% advance without agreement);
- S.14: Compliance with sanctioned plan; structural defects — 5-year warranty;
- S.18: Return of amount + compensation on failure to give possession; interest till handover;
- S.19: Rights and duties of allottees.

Para 10: Alternative remedies — Cite Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd v. Govindan Raghavan (2019) 5 SCC 725 — RERA, Consumer, and Civil court remedies are CONCURRENT, not mutually exclusive. M3M India Pvt Ltd v. Dinesh Sharma (2019) — RERA preferred for matters under the Act. Newtech Promoters v. State of UP (2021) 9 SCC 743 — RERA applies retroactively.
Para 11: Reliefs:
- Possession with delay interest (S.18(1)) — rate at 'such rate as may be prescribed' — typically SBI MCLR + 2% per state Rules.
- Refund (allottee's election) with same rate of interest.
- Completion of promised amenities (S.14).
- Compensation under S.18(3) for mental harassment / financial loss.
- Penalty against promoter under S.59 (non-registration), S.60 (false information), S.61 (other contraventions) — these are penal and discretionary.
Para 12: Where wrongful termination — S.19(6) read with agreement; cite National Buildings Construction Corporation v. Pritam Singh Gill (2020) [where applicable].
Para 13: Where deviation from sanctioned plan — S.14(2): promoter cannot change layout/amenities/specs without consent of 2/3rds of allottees.
Para 14: Where structural defects within 5 years from handover — S.14(3) liability to rectify within 30 days without cost.

Para 15: Appeal — to State Real Estate Appellate Tribunal under S.43-44 within 60 days; further appeal to HC on substantial question of law (S.58) within 60 days. (Pre-deposit may apply for promoter appeals — Newtech Promoters.)
Para 16: Penalty — S.60-72 — penal provisions; complaint can pray for action.

Form fields: typically (i) project name, (ii) RERA registration, (iii) allotment details, (iv) date of agreement, (v) date of possession promised, (vi) date of payment made, (vii) reliefs sought, (viii) consent for online proceedings.
Affidavit in support — mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Liability for false statements in advertisement
Mandatory agreement for sale before accepting >10% advance
Compliance with sanctioned plan + structural defect 5-year warranty
Return of amount + compensation on failure to give possession
Appeal to HC on substantial question of law — 60 days

filing_checklist: Complaint in prescribed form per State RERA Rules (typically Form M)
Vakalatnama / Authorisation in favour of representative
Copy of Agreement for Sale / Allotment Letter
Payment receipts of all instalments paid
RERA project registration certificate / proof of non-registration
Sanctioned plan (if available) for deviation cases
Correspondence with promoter (notices, emails, complaint letters)
ID and address proof of complainant
Filing fee per State RERA Rules (electronically or by DD)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: complainant_name and complainant_address must not be empty
promoter_name and project_name must not be empty
project_rera_registration_no must not be empty (warn if absent — register a complaint under S.59 for non-registration)
agreement_for_sale_date must not be empty and not in future
nature_of_grievance must have at least one selected
previous_consumer_or_civil_proceedings must not be empty (express position)
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format or representative authorisation valid
Court level restricted to State RERA Authority
key_citations: Pioneer Urban Land v. Govindan Raghavan (2019) 5 SCC 725 — Concurrent remedies (RERA / Consumer / Civil)
Newtech Promoters v. State of UP (2021) 9 SCC 743 — RERA retroactive application
Aftab Singh v. Emaar MGF (2019) NCDRC — Concurrent jurisdiction
Forum for People's Collective Efforts v. State of WB (2021) 8 SCC 599 — RERA federal supremacy on real estate
Imperia Structures Ltd v. Anil Patni (2020) 10 SCC 783 — RERA + Consumer concurrent
M3M India Pvt Ltd v. Dinesh Sharma — RERA preferred forum
Wing Commander Arifur Rahman Khan v. DLF Southern Homes (2020) 16 SCC 512 — Reasonable time for possession
